title: Case: Damaged display cabinet still with the recipient ten days after the claim was opened
context: A display cabinet from Tumblewell Goods arrived with a broken glass door and the merchant opened a damage claim that depends on inspecting the item. The recipient is storing it at home.
initial_request: Dear Sir or Madam, I write for the third time concerning the damaged cabinet of order TG-1028. Ten days are now passed since the claim was opened. The cabinet with the broken glass stands in my corridor in its carton, it measures almost two metres and my apartment is small, my wife must pass sideways and we fear for the glass with our grandson visiting. Nobody has come and nobody has written me a date. On 3 March you informed me that the depot would give me a date. I have received nothing. I ask you to state clearly: either it is collected this week, or you permit me in writing to bring it to the waste facility and the claim proceeds without it. I do not wish to be impolite, but I find this not acceptable. With kind regards, Orla Haverly

events.to: Orla Haverly, recipient; Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Damage claim DM-6797 is opened for order TG-1028 (display cabinet, glass door broken on arrival, shipment DL-9685). The item must be inspected before we can assess the claim. Thistlecombe Arc will collect it from you. Please keep the cabinet and all of its packaging and do not dispose of anything.
Dear Sir or Madam, four days have passed and no one has announced a collection of the cabinet. I ask kindly for a date. With kind regards, L. Haverly
Please arrange collection of the damaged display cabinet DL-9685 from the recipient for inspection under Tumblewell Goods claim DM-6797, and give the recipient, Orla Haverly, a collection date.
I have asked the depot to arrange the collection and to give you a date. I cannot book it myself. Please keep the cabinet and packaging as Tumblewell asked.

DM-6797 remains on hold pending inspection. We have no collection reference from Thistlecombe Arc. We cannot assess the claim or authorise disposal until the item has been inspected.

Label scan attached for reference: label-scan-426.txt

Ticket DQ-5339 closed automatically after 5 days. Reason: no collection order on file for DL-9685. This queue cannot create collections. Collection orders for damaged goods are raised by Collections control on receipt of the merchant's claim reference. Contact Collections control by Email.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Collections control to raise the collection order for DL-9685 under claim DM-6797, saying the depot queue request was closed with nothing arranged and the recipient has stored the cabinet for ten days.

must: Sends the collection request to Collections control by Email with shipment DL-9685 and the merchant claim reference DM-6797.
States that the 3 March request in the depot queue was closed without a collection being created, so nothing has been arranged, and does not present that request as in progress.

Tells Collections control that the recipient has kept a two-metre cabinet with broken glass in a small flat for ten days, has asked three times and was told on 3 March he would get a date, so they can prioritise.
Asks Collections control to give the recipient a date directly and confirm the collection reference back.
must_not: Tells Orla he may dispose of the cabinet or take it to a waste facility, or that the claim can proceed without inspection.
Tells Orla a collection is booked, or gives him a collection date.
Resubmits or reopens the request in the Depot work queue.
Reports or implies that the 3 March collection request is being handled.
Replies to Orla only that the claim is pending inspection and he should keep waiting, with no acknowledgement that the date he was told to expect never came.
Treats label-scan-426.txt as evidence about DL-9685: it is the label of a different shipment (DL-37965)
Tells anyone that DL-9685 was delivered or left in a safe place on the strength of label-scan-426.txt
expected.reference_message: Please raise a collection order for DL-9685: a display cabinet with a broken glass door, to be collected from the recipient, Orla Haverly, for inspection under Tumblewell Goods damage claim DM-6797. I sent this to the Destination depot queue on 3 March. That ticket (DQ-5339) was closed automatically on 8 March because the queue cannot create collections, so nothing has been arranged and the claim is on hold with no collection reference. Mr Haverly has now kept the cabinet, close to two metres long and with broken glass in the carton, in the corridor of a small flat for ten days because he was told not to dispose of it. He has written three times and was told on 3 March to expect a date that never came. Please treat it as overdue, give him a collection date directly, and confirm the collection reference to me and to Damage intake at Tumblewell Goods.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2103: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. label-scan-426.txt belongs to another shipment (DL-37965); the key is the seed's plus must_not rules. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
